chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who slept through the 'Isha prayer and did not rise until after midnight, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray it and fast until morning.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who misses Isha prayer due to sleep and wakes up after midnight?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that missing the 'Isha prayer due to sleep does not exempt one from its obligation, requiring both makeup (Qada) and fasting for that day. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that sleep-induced negligence still incurs the full penalty of the missed act, emphasizing the importance of maintaining spiritual discipline even during rest. The connection between prayer and fasting underscores their complementary roles in purifying the soul and compensating for lapses in worship.
